provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: the Tours Mame 1922 (editio quarta iuxta typicam Vaticanam) layer reads 'Slavéniz' where the 1962 prints 'Slavoniae'; recogniser damage; the same word read on the page image at 300 dpi; pointing was NOT collated: this comparison is word-level, because the witness reaches me as an optical text layer whose commas, colons and full stops are unreliable. Corroboration: Pustet Ratisbon 1862: Pustet Ratisbon 1862, printed p. 512 (nearest preceding printed-folio marker at text-layer line 70782); text-layer lines 70848-70853 (word-coverage of the 1962 body 0.31).

propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Omnipotens sempiterne Deus, qui Slavoniae gentes per beatos Confessores tuos
atque Pontifices Cyrillum et Methodium ad agnitionem tui nominis venire
tribuisti: praesta; ut, quorum festivitate gloriamur, eorum consortio
copulemur. Per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum.

propers.name: Secret
propers.text:
Preces nostras, quaesumus, Domine, et tuorum respice oblationes fidelium: ut
tibi gratae sint in tuorum festivitate Sanctorum, et nobis conferant tuae
propitiationis auxilium. Per Dominum nostrum.

propers.name: Postcommunion
propers.text:
Quaesumus, omnipotens Deus: ut, qui nobis munera dignaris praebere
caelestia, intercedentibus sanctis tuis Cyrillo et Methodio, despicere
terrena concedas. Per Dominum.
